title: Regular and finite radicial pullbacks have the same pointwise pinnings
statement:
Let $\ell$ be prime, $n\geq1$, $\Lambda=\mathbf Z/\ell^n\mathbf Z$, and consider morphisms
$$g':Y'\to Y,\qquad h':Y'\to X',\qquad h:Y\to X,\qquad g:X'\to X$$
forming a Cartesian square, so $h\circ g'=g\circ h'$ and $Y'=Y\times_X X'$ with these projections.
All four schemes are Noetherian excellent with $\ell$ invertible [def-exc-excellent-ring]. Assume $h,h'$ are regular, meaning flat with geometrically regular fibres [def-weil-flat-morphism, def-weil-regular-scheme, def-pc-scheme-fibre], and $g,g'$ are finite surjective radicial, meaning finite, surjective and universally injective [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism, def-weil-surjective-morphism, def-weil-radicial-morphism]. Let $K\in D^+(X_{\mathrm{et}},\Lambda)$ have pointwise pinnings $p_x:C_xK\simeq\Lambda(\delta_X(x))[2\delta_X(x)]$ for a dimension function $\delta_X$, without assuming residue compatibility [def-per-potential-dualizing-complex]. Equip $g^!K$ and $g'^!h^*K$ with the finite exceptional pinnings of [lem-per-putative-finite-detection]. For either regular morphism $r:P\to Q$, define its fibrewise pointwise pinnings on $r^*L$ by localizing at $q=r(t)$, using the canonical supported exchange
$$\pi^*C_qL\simeq i^!r^*L$$
for the closed fibre $i:P_q\hookrightarrow P\times_Q\operatorname{Spec}\mathcal O_{Q,q}$ and projection $\pi:P_q\to\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(q)$, applying $p_q$, and then the inverse point Gysin class on the regular fibre [lem-per-regular-supported-base-change, lem-per-prime-power-closed-immersion-gysin]. Its degree at $t$ is $\delta_Q(q)-\dim\mathcal O_{P_q,t}$. Then the canonical isomorphism
$$E_K:h'^*g^!K\xrightarrow{\sim}g'^!h^*K$$
preserves these pointwise pinnings. Here $E_K$ is the tautological comparison under the etale equivalences for the finite universal homeomorphisms $g,g'$: their exceptional inverse images identify with ordinary inverse images, and the two ordinary inverse-image composites identify by the Cartesian square. The Gysin degree factors in the induced finite pinnings are retained; the assertion does not replace finite purely inseparable Gysin maps by identities.

source.place: Expose XVII, Lemma 4.3.2.2 (statement and field-degree proof), with the pointwise constructions of Lemma 4.3.1.1 and Proposition 2.4.3.1.

proof.text: Use [lem-per-regular-supported-base-change] to express each regular-pullback costalk as the costalk, on the regular fibre, of the pullback of the base costalk. Apply its given pinning and then the inverse point class of [lem-per-prime-power-closed-immersion-gysin]. This is exactly the fibrewise construction in the statement. The finite exceptional pinnings are those of [lem-per-putative-finite-detection]: at a residue-field map $a$ they apply $a^!p$ followed by $\operatorname{Cl}_a^{-1}$. In particular the pinning contains the inverse of the Gysin degree, rather than discarding that factor.

The finite maps $g,g'$ are integral by [pqf-lem-finite-integral-lft], and are surjective and universally injective, so [lem-pc-integral-radicial-surjective-universal-homeomorphism] makes them universal homeomorphisms. By [thm-weil-pbc-universal-homeomorphism-invariance], ordinary inverse and direct images are inverse equivalences. The same equivalences apply to constant-$\Lambda$ modules, and termwise to complexes: an additive equivalence preserves kernels and cokernels, hence quasi-isomorphisms. A finite map is proper by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-proper], so its compactification with identity open part gives $Rg_!=Rg_*$ by [def-amb-etale-compact-support]. Uniqueness of right adjoints [det-sp-unique-right-adjoint] therefore identifies $g^!$ with $g^*$, and likewise for $g'$. The coherent composition comparisons of [lem-weil-pbc-derived-inverse-image-composition] identify the two composites around the Cartesian square, giving precisely $E_K$.

source.place: XVII, Lemma 4.3.2.2: the evident underlying isomorphism

proof.text: Fix $x\in X$ and its unique inverse image $x'\in X'$, and put $E=\kappa(x)$, $E'=\kappa(x')$, $V=Y_x$, $V'=Y'_{x'}$. Then $V'=V\times_E E'$. Supported exchange, including its compatibility with successive supported restrictions [lem-per-regular-supported-base-change], and finite exceptional fibre/costalk transitivity [lem-per-prime-power-supported-calculus] identify the two pinning composites over these fibres with those for the square $V'\to V$ over $\operatorname{Spec}E'\to\operatorname{Spec}E$, with base object $C_xK$. The finite pinning on $C_{x'}g^!K$ is the one on $a^!C_xK$ of [lem-per-putative-finite-detection]. These identifications are natural and have the right-adjoint composition normalization, so Step 2's comparison is unchanged. Apply $p_x$ to replace $C_xK$ by $\Lambda_E(m)[2m]$, $m=\delta_X(x)$. The fibres are Noetherian excellent (affine locally a quotient of a localization of an excellent ring, by [lem-exc-finite-type-localization-excellent]) and regular by geometric regularity. We have reduced only the base to fields, not arbitrary points of $V$ to residue fields.

source.place: XVII, Lemma 4.3.2.2, first reduction to the fields E and E′

proof.text: On this field-base square, decompose the regular schemes into open and closed integral components using [rem-pc-regular-normal]. The right-hand regular pullback is $\Lambda_V(m)[2m]$ with the canonical regular pinnings: [lem-per-prime-power-closed-immersion-gysin] identifies their point maps with the inverse point classes, and [lem-per-potential-dualizing-regular-unit] makes them potential. Finite surjective detection [lem-per-putative-finite-detection] then makes its exceptional pullback to $V'$ potential. On the other side, $a^!\Lambda_E(m)[2m]$ is a constant Tate line by Step 2; its given pinning is a scalar normalization. Pulling it to $V'$ by the displayed regular-fibre construction therefore gives the canonical regular pinnings, all multiplied by that same scalar, and these are potential by [lem-per-potential-dualizing-regular-unit]. Their dimension functions agree: $V'\to V$ is a homeomorphism, preserving prime chains and hence local codimensions on these regular components. Both functions are $m$ minus that codimension.

source.place: XVII, Lemma 4.3.2.2: both fibrewise objects are potential, using Propositions 2.4.4.1 and 2.4.3.3

proof.text: It now suffices to check $E_K$ at generic points of $V'$. Here is the propagation argument, rather than assuming this reduction for putative complexes. At a geometric point $z$, let $b_z\in\Lambda^\times$ be the ratio between the target pinning composed with $C_z(E_K)$ and the source pinning. Both are isomorphisms to the same Tate line. Naturality of the residue transitions in [lem-per-higher-residue-transitivity], and potentiality from Step 4 in the sense of [def-per-potential-dualizing-complex], imply $b_u=b_v$ for every immediate geometric specialization $u\rightsquigarrow v$: in the pinning coordinates its transition is the identity on the corresponding rank-one cohomology groups. For any point choose a generic generization in its component and a geometric specialization above it. The finite factorization into immediate specializations and codimension-zero transport supplied by [lem-per-higher-residue-transitivity] shows that its ratio equals the generic ratio. Consequently ratios equal to $1$ at the generic points equal $1$ everywhere. This uses potentiality only after the base-field reduction, never potentiality of the original $K$.

source.place: XVII, Lemma 4.3.2.2, reduction to maximal points; Theorem 3.1.2

proof.text: Localize $V$ at the generic point corresponding to the chosen generic point of $V'$. By [rem-pc-regular-normal] and regularity these generic local schemes are fields: write $V=\operatorname{Spec}F$. The Cartesian inverse image has algebra $F\otimes_EE'$, finite over $F$; it is regular by localization [lem-weil-pbc-regular-local-localization] and has one point since $V'\to V$ is a universal homeomorphism. A zero-dimensional regular local ring has maximal ideal generated by zero elements and is a field. Thus $V'=\operatorname{Spec}F'$ with $F'=F\otimes_EE'$. Tensoring an $E$-basis of $E'$ with $F$ gives $[F':F]=[E':E]=e$. These finite residue extensions are purely inseparable by [def-weil-radicial-morphism]. By [lem-per-prime-power-regular-gysin], both finite field Gysin classes are multiplication by $e$ under the tautological etale equivalences, so their inverse classes in the pinnings are both $e^{-1}$. The regular generic pinnings are the identity by [lem-per-potential-dualizing-regular-unit]. Hence the two generic pinning composites are the same scalar $e^{-1}$ on the pullback of the base Tate line. Step 2 identifies their underlying line maps by the canonical composition comparison, so their ratio is $1$.

source.place: XVII, Lemma 4.3.2.2, generic-field tensor product and equality of degrees

proof.text: Step 5 extends the generic equality of Step 6 to all points of every field-base fibre. The supported identifications of Step 3 and the pinning construction of Step 1 then give equality at every point of $Y'$, which says exactly that $E_K$ preserves the stated pinnings. Empty fibres contribute no points. The argument retains the finite purely inseparable degree factors and assumes no residue compatibility of $K$.

split_report.summary: Resumed the retained split and searches. The initial dry run found a missing citation quote. Source review also found an invalid reduction to arbitrary residue fields: their tensor product can be nonreduced. Restored ILO XVII Lemma 4.3.2.2: reduce the base to fields, establish potentiality of both fibre objects using canonical regular pinnings and finite detection, propagate pinning equality from generic points by natural residue transitions, and only then compute the field degrees. Seven steps, no new nodes; statement unchanged.

tool_uses.why: Generic scheme-theoretic fact that integral, universally injective, surjective maps are universal homeomorphisms; the perverse unit has no replacement for this etale-topos input.
Generic etale-topos invariance under universal homeomorphisms, used to identify finite exceptional inverse images with ordinary inverse images; no unit-local substitute states this equivalence.
Generic uniqueness of right adjoints, used to identify the exceptional right adjoint with the inverse equivalence under the universal-homeomorphism etale equivalence.
Generic coherence of derived inverse-image composition, used for the Cartesian comparison E_K; the unit route supplies no separate derived pseudofunctor node.
Generic regular-scheme component decomposition, used to work on connected integral regular fibres; this is a scheme-theoretic tool, not a replacement of the unit route.
Generic excellence preservation under localization and finite-type quotients, ensuring the fibre schemes satisfy the potential-pinning hypotheses.
Chosen-compactification definition used with identity open part to identify finite compact support with direct image.
Generic localization of regular local rings, used to show the generic finite field-base-change algebra is regular.
Finite implies integral, used to apply the universal-homeomorphism criterion.
Finite implies proper, used for the identity-open compactification computing finite compact support.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q39-4ff410c78 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read the 7-step split in full against ILO XVII Lemma 4.3.2.2 (p.284), Lemmas 4.3.1.1–4.3.1.2 (pp.282–283) and the 4.3.2.1 invocation. The delivery has no new nodes and the statement is unchanged; it is the Z/ℓ^n version of 4.1.1 and 4.3.2.2, keeps the inseparable-degree factors, and is not weakened. Step 1: the pinning construction matches the cited regular-supported-base-change, closed-immersion-gysin 'Regular pinnings' and putative-finite-detection (Cl_a^{-1}∘a^!p) statements. Step 2: g^!≅g^* follows from finite⇒integral⇒universal homeomorphism (radicial + surjective), the topos equivalence, Rg_!=g_* (finite⇒proper) and uniqueness of right adjoints; the composite is the 'isomorphisme évident'. Step 3: the base is reduced to fields with V'=V×_E E'; the fibres are excellent as localizations of B/pB, and regular because h is regular. Step 4: Λ_V(m)[2m] is potential on each component by regular-unit and rem-pc-regular-normal; finite-surjective detection makes its pullback to V' potential; the dimension functions agree since V'→V is a homeomorphism. Step 5: I checked the ratio b_z∈Λ^× argument: b_y=b_x follows from the residue equation of def-per-potential-dualizing-complex for both potential pinnings, and the chain factorization is the last clause of higher-residue-transitivity. Step 6: the generic local ring is a field F; the localization of V' at the generic point is F⊗_E E', which is regular, 0-dimensional and local, hence a field; [F':F]=[E':E]=e; both classes are e (prime-power-regular-gysin), so both composites are e^{-1}. Small case E=F_p(s), E'=E(s^{1/p}), V=A^1: at the closed point t^p=s the residue degree is 1 while [E':E]=p, so the worker's correction (propagate from generic points) is necessary and correct. I also checked g=id, n=1, disconnected and empty fibres. No duplicate of this Z/ℓ^n 4.3.2.2 statement (grep '4.3.2.2' and 'radicial'), no cycle, no SGA citation. I accept all 10 generic tool_uses. Batch 5: I recomputed the closure from the two targets, stopping at the nt-assume leaves; adding the item's proof_deps adds 0 nodes (16546 nodes either way), and all four flagged citations are already in the closure. The trf endpoints are general results, not steps of the trace formula or Poincaré duality proofs: ind-étale strict-local invariance (Stacks 05WR), finite-base strict localization, the D^+ adjunction, and the smooth orientation, which this item does not use because it takes only the inseparable-degree clause. Maintainer note, a gap across the whole DAG and not this delivery's fault: Step 6 identifies Cl_π of absolute-gysin-purity (used by the finite-detection pinnings) with the class of prime-power-regular-gysin. No citable node states this; finite-surjective-potential-detection does, but citing it would make a cycle. The same note was accepted for Q18 (9764cb95). No fixes.
